endorsements.quote: Data governance policies and procedures must be established before building an infrastructure for federated learning.
Depending on the jurisdiction and type of data involved, there may be legal and regulatory requirements governing the de-identification of data.
To be secured against unauthorized access and other security threats, implementing access controls, encryption and other security measures can protect sensitive data.
In addition, the import of data from internal clinical systems such as the hospital information system (HIS), the radiological information system (RIS) and PACS must be guaranteed.

unlisted_practices: Integrate the federated learning local node into the existing clinical IT infrastructure rather than a separate departmental environment, unless specifications cannot be met.
Establish a Joint Controllership Agreement defining data handling, de-identification, and data sharing rules among federated network partners.
Use strong pseudonymization with re-identification keys kept on local servers and never shared with partners or third parties.
Document the data model and associated metadata when sharing data so other parties can interpret it.
Ensure local nodes have sufficient hardware resources and reliable network connectivity for the expected workload.
Establish secure connections and authentication between the PACS and local federated learning services.
Run local node applications in virtual machines or containers to create standardized, isolated environments.
Design federated learning models to accommodate heterogeneity of datasets across institutions.
Evaluate the global federated model on each local node to assess performance on diverse datasets.
Ensure congruence of local nodes with the network's technical standards to guarantee interfaces for data transfer and updates.

screen.reason: Technical note and guideline/recommendations outlining infrastructure requirements and governance for implementing local nodes in a federated machine learning network for radiology.
